items.readable_text:
Content:
Notice that if we split an equilateral triangle in half, we get two [MATH: 30^\circ]-[MATH: 60^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangles. We can use this idea to compute the area of an equilateral triangle.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/67c941733b18a19a261d0429a9c57888]

Content:
As shown in the above diagram, if the equilateral has side length [MATH: s,] then according to the side length ratios of the [MATH: 30^\circ]-[MATH: 60^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangle, the height of the equilateral triangle is [MATH: \dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2} s.]

Content:
So, the area of the equilateral triangle is

Content:
[MATH: A|= (1)/(2) ⋅ s ⋅ (sqrt(3))/(2)s; = (sqrt(3))/(4)s^{2}.]

[MATH: A|= (sqrt(3))/(4) ⋅ 8^{2}; = (sqrt(3))/(4) ⋅ 64; = 16sqrt(3).]
